gaugeContext.note: USGS 05342000 measures the lower Kinni at County F. The reading provides river conditions; it does not measure travel speed, the dam-side launch, or St. Croix backwater and wind effects near the beach.

timing.note: No reviewed flow-to-speed calibration is assigned. The County F outfitter time is separate planning guidance; no live ETA or GPS time remaining is calculated.

blurb: The lower Kinni near River Falls: a popular gorge paddle below Powell Falls Dam to County F, with a longer option to the St. Croix beach. Expect moving water, rapids and hand-carried boats. This is the St. Croix tributary, separate from Milwaukee’s Kinnickinnic River.

sections.notes: A wooded gorge paddle with frequent riffles, rapids, sharp bends and fallen-tree hazards. Carry in below the dam and finish at County F. The local outfitter recommends intermediate to advanced paddlers; expect to maneuver or carry around obstacles. This is not a passive tubing itinerary.

distanceEvidence.note: Approximate published trip distance. The source reports 7.5 miles; an independent USGS centerline measures about 7.4 miles before the dam-side approach is omitted. Another firsthand report has an 8.1-mile summary but calls the trip 7.5 miles in its narrative. Retain 7.5 miles for planning; do not substitute the shorter displayed overview length. Parking carries are excluded.

notices.title: Start below Powell Falls Dam
notices.text: DNR still lists Powell Falls Dam as present. Carry to the lower-river launch and stay clear of the spillway. Restoration plans do not establish that the dam has been removed; check city updates and posted access signs before your trip.

notices.title: State park parking admission
notices.text: A vehicle admission pass is required at the state park takeouts. Arrange your shuttle before launching; the County F anglers lot and the main park beach parking are different destinations.

guideTimes.conditions: Local outfitter’s average for the Lower Canyon solo-kayak trip to County F. Its schedule allows an additional hour for leisure stops. This is planning guidance, not a live-flow estimate, and excludes your vehicle shuttle.

sections.routeReview: The dotted overview begins downstream of the immediate Powell Falls spillway approach. Exact launch and landing connections are not mapped; follow the access directions and current signs.

putInAccess.accessType: Informal carry-in boat launch below Powell Falls Dam
putInAccess.sourceName: City of River Falls — Recreation Facilities Inventory, January 2020, table 2
putInAccess.note: The city inventory identifies this coordinate specifically as the informal carry-in boat launch (printed page 15, table 2), separate from the fishing area, bench and trails. The coordinate is unchanged from that inventory and was checked against the city trail map and satellite imagery. It replaces the older guide-area pin about 26 metres upstream. This is a desktop source review, not a current inspection of landing conditions. Future restoration plans do not establish that the dam has been removed.
putInAccess.directions: From the Glen Park parking area near the pickleball courts on West Park Street, carry your boat down the steep trail to the city’s informal launch below Powell Falls Dam. The pin marks the documented boat launch on the south bank, not parking. Stay clear of the spillway and check posted access signs.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: Kinni Creek Lodge and Outfitters — Lower Canyon takeout; Wisconsin DNR — park map
takeOutAccess.note: The DNR park map and current outfitter itinerary identify this takeout. The unchanged Miles Paddled coordinate sits on the bank near the parking approach, not at a surveyed water-edge landing. Satellite context agrees with the bridge and lot. Keep it approximate; it is unrelated to the Kinnickinnic River in Milwaukee.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use the Anglers Parking Lot beside County F, separate from the main park entrance. Inspect the bank access beside the bridge while arranging your shuttle. The park map identifies the lot; current outfitter instructions use it for the Lower Canyon takeout. A state park vehicle admission pass is required.

sections.notes: Continue past County F toward the St. Croix and finish at the state park beach. Current slows on the lower reach, and the final approach may involve wind, wakes and paddling along the St. Croix shore. Plan for the uphill boat carry; the County F three-hour guide does not cover this longer trip.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: Wisconsin DNR — Kinnickinnic State Park map; Miles Paddled — 2018 trip
takeOutAccess.note: DNR maps the beach, paved Black Trail and uphill parking. Miles Paddled documents a trip ending here, but its unchanged 2018 coordinate lies on the sand rather than identifying the paved trail connection. Keep the beach-area marker approximate; beach shape and water level can change. This is not a trailer ramp.
takeOutAccess.directions: At the Kinni mouth, follow the Wisconsin shoreline toward the park beach north of the confluence. Locate the paved Black Trail connection and allow for a steep carry uphill to the St. Croix picnic-area parking. Vehicles cannot be brought down to the beach. Check the exit before launching and arrange a shuttle.

mapAuditNote: Two published lower-river trips have reviewed access-area maps. Exact water-edge landings remain approximate and open to reviewed community corrections.
